main.title: Diana: her death and the public mourning
main.summary: Diana, Princess of Wales, died after a car crash in Paris on 31 August 1997.

cards.heading: Diana: her death and the public mourning
cards.text: Diana, Princess of Wales, died after a car crash in Paris on 31 August 1997. The news prompted widespread public mourning for a woman whose royal role, activism and public image had made her internationally known. Her marriage to Prince Charles in 1981 had brought her into the centre of public attention, followed by the births of William and Harry. The couple separated in 1992 as the breakdown of their relationship became public. Her death brought that intensely observed life to a sudden end and produced an extensive collective response.

main.title: OK Computer
main.summary: OK Computer is the third studio album by the English rock band Radiohead, released on 21 May 1997.

cards.heading: OK Computer
cards.text:
OK Computer is the third studio album by the English rock band Radiohead, released on 21 May 1997. With their producer, Nigel Godrich, Radiohead recorded most of OK Computer in their rehearsal space in Oxfordshire and the historic mansion of St Catherine's Court in Bath in 1996 and early 1997. They distanced themselves from the guitar-centred and lyrically introspective style of their previous album, The Bends. OK Computer's abstract lyrics, densely layered sound and eclectic influences laid the groundwork for Radiohead's later, more experimental work.

The lyrics depict a dystopian world fraught with rampant consumerism, social alienation, technological anxiety and political corruption, while also exploring themes of transport, conformity, paranoia, death, modern British life and globalisation. In this capacity, OK Computer is said to have prescient insight into the mood of 21st-century life. Radiohead used unconventional production techniques, including natural reverberation, and used few overdubs. Strings were recorded at Abbey Road Studios in London.

main.title: Titanic
main.summary: Titanic is a 1997 American epic historical romance film written and directed by James Cameron.

cards.heading: Titanic
cards.text:
Titanic is a 1997 American epic historical romance film written and directed by James Cameron. Incorporating both historical and fictional aspects, it is based on accounts of the sinking of RMS Titanic in 1912. Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet star as members of different social classes who fall in love during the ship's ill-fated maiden voyage. The ensemble cast includes Billy Zane, Kathy Bates, Frances Fisher, Bernard Hill, Jonathan Hyde, Danny Nucci, David Warner and Bill Paxton.

Cameron's inspiration came from his fascination with shipwrecks. He felt a love story interspersed with human loss would be essential to convey the emotional impact of the disaster. Production began on September 1, 1995, when Cameron shot footage of the Titanic wreck. The modern scenes were shot on board the Shirshov Institute of Oceanology research vessel Akademik Mstislav Keldysh, which Cameron had used as a base when filming the wreck. Scale models, computer-generated imagery (CGI), and a reconstruction of the Titanic built at Baja Studios were used to recreate the sinking.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
main.summary: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone is J. K. Rowling's debut fantasy novel, published by Bloomsbury in 1997, introducing Harry, Hogwarts, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger.

cards.heading: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
cards.text:
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone is a fantasy novel by British author J. K. Rowling. It is the first novel in the Harry Potter series and was Rowling's debut novel. It follows Harry Potter, a young wizard who discovers his magical heritage on his eleventh birthday when he receives a letter of acceptance from Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. With the help of his friends, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, Harry unravels a mystery involving the dark wizard Lord Voldemort.

The book was first published in the United Kingdom on 26 June 1997 by Bloomsbury. It was published in the United States the following year by Scholastic Corporation under the title Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone. It won most of the British book awards that were judged by children and other awards in the US. The book reached the top of the New York Times list of best-selling fiction in August 1999, and stayed near the top of that list for much of 1999 and 2000.

main.title: Cowboy Bebop
main.summary: Cowboy Bebop began airing in 1998, following a crew of bounty hunters travelling aboard the Bebop in 2071.

cards.heading: Cowboy Bebop
cards.text: Cowboy Bebop began airing in 1998, following a crew of bounty hunters travelling aboard the Bebop in 2071. Director Shinichirō Watanabe and writer Keiko Nobumoto combined science fiction with Western and noir influences across twenty-six episodes, called sessions. Yoko Kanno's music became a central part of the series' identity. Individual jobs reveal characters struggling with loneliness and histories they cannot easily leave behind. Sunrise's animation and the mixture of genres found audiences in Japan and abroad, particularly in the United States, where the series helped broaden the international audience for anime.

main.title: iMac G3
main.summary: The iMac G3, originally released as the iMac, is a series of Macintosh personal computers that Apple Computer sold from 1998 to 2003.

cards.heading: iMac G3
cards.text:
The iMac G3, originally released as the iMac, is a series of Macintosh personal computers that Apple Computer sold from 1998 to 2003. The iMac was Apple's first major product release under CEO Steve Jobs following his return to the financially troubled company he co-founded. Jobs reorganized the company and simplified the product line. The iMac was designed as Apple's new consumer desktop product—an inexpensive, consumer-oriented computer that would easily connect to the Internet.

The iMac's all-in-one design is based around a cathode-ray tube display; the G3 processor, components, and connectivity were all included in a single enclosure. Apple's head of design Jony Ive and his team developed a teardrop-shaped, translucent plastic case that was a radical departure from the look of the company's previous computers. The company developed new working methods to finish the computer quickly, and new workflows for designing future products. The iMac eschewed legacy technologies like serial ports and floppy disk drives in favor of CD-ROMs and USB ports.

main.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
main.subtitle: Rumours spread through Hogwarts in Harry's second year
main.summary: Published by Bloomsbury on 2 July 1998, J.K. Rowling's second Harry Potter novel makes the school itself the scene of an investigation. Attacks leave pupils petrified, and rumours about a hidden chamber turn classmates against one another. Harry's unusual ability to understand snakes makes him an object of suspicion. Alongside Ron and Hermione, he searches for an explanation in the history of Hogwarts. Dobby's warnings and Gilderoy Lockhart's self-promotion add two very different kinds of unreliable guidance to the mystery.

cards.heading: A school under suspicion
cards.text: Published by Bloomsbury on 2 July 1998, J.K. Rowling's second Harry Potter novel makes the school itself the scene of an investigation. Attacks leave pupils petrified, and rumours about a hidden chamber turn classmates against one another. Harry's unusual ability to understand snakes makes him an object of suspicion. Alongside Ron and Hermione, he searches for an explanation in the history of Hogwarts. Dobby's warnings and Gilderoy Lockhart's self-promotion add two very different kinds of unreliable guidance to the mystery.

cards.heading: The past writes back
cards.text: A diary introduces a more intimate way for the past to intrude on the school year. Harry can write questions into it and receive answers, making an apparently ordinary object into a source he must decide whether to trust. Elsewhere, talk of magical ancestry determines how pupils are treated and who is thought to belong. These threads connect the hidden danger to everyday prejudice, while Rowling keeps the investigation moving through lessons, Quidditch and the friends' attempts to uncover information without being caught.

main.title: GeForce 256
main.summary: The GeForce 256 is the original release in Nvidia's "GeForce" product line.

cards.heading: GeForce 256
cards.text: The GeForce 256 is the original release in Nvidia's "GeForce" product line. Announced on August 31, 1999 and released on October 11, 1999, the GeForce 256 improves on its predecessor (RIVA TNT2) by increasing the number of fixed pixel pipelines, offloading host geometry calculations to a hardware transform and lighting (T&L) engine, and adding hardware motion compensation for MPEG-2 video. It offered a notable leap in 3D PC gaming performance and was the first fully Direct3D 7-compliant 3D accelerator.

main.title: Napster
main.summary: Napster was a proprietary peer-to-peer file sharing application primarily associated with the distribution of digital audio files such as MP3s.

cards.heading: Napster
cards.text:
Napster was a proprietary peer-to-peer file sharing application primarily associated with the distribution of digital audio files such as MP3s. It was launched in June 1999 by Shawn Fanning and Sean Parker. Due to lawsuits alleging copyright infringement, Napster was shut down in July 2001 and filed for bankruptcy in June 2002.

Napster's intellectual property was acquired by Roxio for $5.3 million in November 2002 and it was relaunched under a subscription business model. In September 2008, Napster was purchased by Best Buy for $121 million. It was sold to Rhapsody in December 2011. In 2016, Rhapsody was renamed Napster. In 2022, Napster was acquired by two Web3 companies, Hivemind and Algorand. In March 2025, Napster was sold to Infinite Reality. In 2026, it was relaunched as an artificial intelligence tool.

main.title: The Matrix
main.summary: The Matrix reached cinemas in 1999, following hacker Neo as he discovers that intelligent machines have constructed the reality around him.

cards.heading: The Matrix
cards.text: The Matrix reached cinemas in 1999, following hacker Neo as he discovers that intelligent machines have constructed the reality around him. Morpheus and Trinity recruit him into a rebellion against that system. The Wachowskis combined cyberpunk ideas with action shaped by anime and Hong Kong martial-arts choreography. The film's bullet-time effect lets the camera appear to move around action unfolding in slow motion, giving Neo's changing perception a visible form. Its red-pill choice and distinctive fight scenes carried the story's questions about control and reality into popular culture.
